answer: Make standing sail an ocean no farm can flood: a newcomer must cross between ivory buoys anchored far apart, each buoy stamping a violet tide-mark only while the current runs in its favour, so a crossing takes real time and cannot be rushed or copied. Marks bind to one key and expire with the tide, and standing grows only as fresh marks accumulate across many buoys. Random harbour audits re-check buoy logs, freezing identities whose marks repeat routes or crews. Sybil farms must fund a crossing, chase every tide, and pass fresh buoys for every clone, costing more than honest work pays.
